text:
maria_support: Heads up — Customer `acme-42` is hitting 429s in production. Started ~08:45 UTC, steady stream of errors across regions (us-west1, eu-west1). Customer reports ~120 TPS bursts from a worker pool. Error body below from their dev:
customer_jen: Posting payload they get back from our API:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1678902345
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "message": "Rate limit exceeded: requests per minute (RPM) quota hit"
  }
}
```
maria_support: They included a curl repro too — calling our v1/generate endpoint in parallel from 8 workers. They claim they didn't change traffic pattern but a scheduled job may have kicked off.
ajay_oncall: @maria_support can you paste the org+project id? I want to check the quota config and recent token-level headers from our nginx/edge layer. Also which API key they use (prod vs test)?
maria_support: Org `acme-42`, project `prod-main`, api_key suffix `-prod345`. Customer says it's the prod key — they've got reserved burst windows historically but maybe it expired.
lizze_eng: Quick checklist: 1) check X-RateLimit headers in our ingress logs to confirm whether RPM or TPM was exceeded; 2) inspect our quota service for any recent policy change; 3) look at recent deploys and config flips. I can pull the ingress logs.\
\deploy-bot: Deployed commit 8f2ab3 to infra/proxy at 2026-03-15T07:50:12Z (rollout v1.43.2). No config changes to rate-limiter in this deploy. :package:
ajay_oncall: I'm tailing the edge logs now. Found this series around 08:46:12 UTC:
```
[08:46:11] request_id=abc123 method=POST path=/v1/generate api_key=***-prod345 status=200 latency_ms=45
[08:46:11] request_id=abc124 method=POST path=/v1/generate api_key=***-prod345 status=200 latency_ms=48
[08:46:12] request_id=abc130 method=POST path=/v1/generate api_key=***-prod345 status=429 latency_ms=5 rate_limit_limit=1200 rate_limit_remaining=0 reset=1764829160
[08:46:12] request_id=abc131 method=POST path=/v1/generate api_key=***-prod345 status=429 latency_ms=3 rate_limit_limit=1200 rate_limit_remaining=0 reset=1764829160
```
ajay_oncall: Looks like per-minute quota hit (RPM). The limit for that key currently returns 1200 (RPM). If they sent ~120 TPS sustained for ~10s, they'll hit per-minute envelope quickly. Need to confirm their bursts produce >1200 requests in that rolling minute.
jonah_success: Customer comments: "We have a worker fleet that fans out to 10k users during reports generation — we thought our backoff in the client would smooth it but apparently not." They asked if we can temporarily raise RPM while they patch their clients.
lizze_eng: Two mitigation options: 1) short-term: temporarily increase RPM for org `acme-42` (we can grant a burst allowance or raise the quota for 1 hour). 2) longer-term: recommend they adopt token-level client-side leaky-bucket with jittered exponential backoff and switch to batched requests or stream generation if they're doing many small calls.
maria_support: Customer requested emergency bump. Can ops approve a 2x for 1 hour? They need to complete a reporting window in the next 20–30 minutes.
ajay_oncall: I'll open a quick ticket to quota-service to apply a temporary override. @lizze_eng can you prepare rollback/monitoring so we auto-revert? Also enable an alert if TTL not cleared.
lizze_eng: On it — I'll add a temporary override with a 1-hour TTL and set a metric alert if usage exceeds 90% of the new limit. Patch will include audit entry. Steps: use internal admin UI -> Quotas -> Org `acme-42` -> Override RPM=2400 TTL=1h reason="prod spike - emergency bump". I'll post confirmation.
ops_tooling_bot: Quota override request created: id=qov-7891 by ajay_oncall. Status=PENDING_APPROVAL. Link: https://admin.internal/quotas/qov-7891
maria_support: Customer is standing by; they want to know estimated time to apply.
ajay_oncall: Approving now. Also adding note: we should watch token-level Remaining headers and queue a rollback if they keep hitting limits.
ops_tooling_bot: Quota override qov-7891 approved by ajay_oncall. Override applied: RPM=2400 for org=acme-42 until 1764832702. Audit: ajay_oncall.

customer_jen: Confirmed — traffic is flowing again, errors dropped within 30s. Thank you!! :tada:
lizze_eng: Follow-ups: 1) recommend they patch client to use exponential backoff and avoid synchronized bursts (randomized jitter). 2) recommend they batch small prompts into a single request if possible. 3) offer guided review of their worker scheduling.
ajay_oncall: We'll also add a note to the account: "one-hour emergency RPM bump applied 2026-03-15 08:51 UTC; recommend quota review and plan upgrade if this pattern recurs."
maria_support: Customer asked for a short playbook for handling 429s. I'm pasting a condensed troubleshooting checklist we use:
- Confirm X-RateLimit headers and whether Remaining==0
- Check edge logs for token and org spikes (request_id samples)
- Verify whether RPM vs TPM vs per-second limits triggered (headers & quota-service)
- If immediate impact: consider temporary quota override (with TTL) or route traffic to dedicated capacity if available
- Always recommend client-side backoff + jitter and request batching
- For repeated incidents: propose capacity plan or Dedicated allocation

jonah_success: I'll send that checklist to the customer and propose a 1:1 to review their workload scheduling. Nice fast triage, team.
lizze_eng: Action items captured: 1) lizze to add TTL + monitoring on override (done). 2) ajay to update account note (done). 3) maria to share 429 playbook with customer + schedule follow-up call. 4) eng to look at ingress pattern detection to auto-detect synchronized fan-outs.
maria_support: Closing thread once the customer confirms no more 429s in the next 24h. Thanks everyone. :pray:

customer_jen: All green on our end. We'll follow up with logs and plan to implement jitter within 48h. Appreciate the quick assist!"
